text:
anna_s: Heads up — seeing ~2.5x tail latency spike on FlashAttn-paged when KV cache hit rate dips below ~85%. Repro in prod canary this morning. Can dump traces if helpful.

tom_k: hmm. do you have the perf flame? could be shared memory bank conflicts from the dynamic tiling path. :thinking_face:

anna_s: pasted light profiler snapshot: 
```
SM0: shared_load=1.2GB/s shared_store=1.1GB/s gmem_load=4.5GB/s
warp_occupancy=0.62 l2_hitrate=0.88 kv_hits=0.79
avg_latency_per_token=0.87ms
spill_regs=24 spill_mem=3MB
```

lia_m: paging the cached KV pages changes buffer alignment and invalidates our pipeline stages — that can cause bank thrash. try tile_k 64->128 and drop pipeline_stages to 2 in the paged kernel to see if it stabilizes.

tom_k: ran a quick A/B on dev: flashattn-paged-v2 (tile=64) vs fused variant (tile=128). fused reduces p95 by ~18% and increases throughput ~4%, but uses more registers causing extra spills on A100 40GB when seq_len<128.

devon_p: batching heuristics also matter here — the auto-batcher was emitting a lot of small micro-batches. raising batch_min from 8->12 smoothed variance and dropped tail.

perf-bot: benchmark summary (run=2025-05-03T19:02Z):
- model: redwood/opt-6b-qlora
- workload: mixed chat (seq=256-1024), kv_cache hitting 70-95%
- kernels: flashattn-paged-v2 (tiling=64) vs flashattn-fused (tiling=128)
- p95 latency: 122ms -> 100ms (fused)
- throughput tok/s: 6800 -> 7200
- noted: fused increased reg usage by ~8, occasional spills in narrow cases

anna_s: ok i'll roll a canary with tile=128 + pipeline=2 + batch_min=12 and monitor for regressions. i'll also enable the perf-trace flag for a 30-min window. :rocket:

tom_k: also add a kernel-selector rule: prefer fused if kv_hit_rate < 0.9 AND seq_len > 512; otherwise prefer paged. that avoids fused's reg pressure for short sequences.

lia_m: occupancy tuning note: cap per-thread regs to avoid spills; try max_regs_per_thread=64 for the fused kernel config. also consider lowering threads_per_warp_block to increase occupancy if we see underutilization.

devon_p: if we still see spikes after canary, fallback plan is to pin to flashattn-paged-tiling=64 with kv-threshold=0.8 until we have a refined tiling/pipeline heuristic.

anna_s: canary results after 20m: p95 down ~12%, kv hit ratio stable, cpu-side mem copies reduced, no OOMs. looks good so far — closing this investigation for now. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
